While I'm going to side with Atko on the technical issues with the rule as it was, I think something like it should definitely be a part of voat.

When I read Atko's statement, it seemed like a decision made out of a non-existent necessity. While I understand that it was made due to the aforementioned social bypasses being run on certain subverses (threads meant for nothing more than CCP-mongering), that was at least confined to small, isolated instances of trying to game the old system. It meant limited brigading could be done if/when it was done, and that certain users who gained CCP and SCP could easily be identified thanks to Voat's transparent user history. Now, however, anyone can downvoat anyone else with little to no effort needed, which leads to the exact same issue that Reddit has and always had: all it takes is a group concentrating enough to completely obliterate a post they don't like for little to no reason.

While there might be a new system coming to prevent such a thing, I have to disagree with the decision made and echo what a lot of other users have said in the announcement thread:** leave the old system in until such a time as the new one can be implemented**. It shouldn't matter who complains about the 100 CCP requirement, how many messages you get or whining goes on in a subverse, or what it means that 'x' number of users can't downvoat something. Having that limit on downvoating was an essential tool not only for preventing brigades, but also to foster a community that would learn that having the power to say "this contributes nothing" should come from creating content or making a comment that does contribute something.

But that's just my two cents.
